title: Medical AI is already in hospitals, but most of the devices haven't been properly tested
key_facts: Census by Rawan Abulibdeh (University of Toronto) and MIT Critical Data colleagues, in PLOS Digital Health
1,357 AI devices cleared or approved by FDA through 5 Dec 2025
34 had a registered trial; 3 studied patient outcomes
94% of the 34 trials run by the manufacturer; 73.5% enrolled under 500 people
1,059 devices read images, only 3 of them with a registered trial
Most reach market via the 510(k) route (similarity to an existing device)
Limit: unregistered private studies would not show up; no non-AI comparison group
Sepsis tool missed 67% of cases in a 2021 outside test
quote_evidence: Of 1,357 AI devices the FDA has cleared for use in patient care, three were tested on whether patients lived longer or better.
Untested doesn't mean unsafe, and the authors are careful about that.
The full study was published in the journal PLOS Digital Health.
why_it_matters_hint: Clearance does not show patient benefit; evidence gap is large.
notes: Earth.com interviewed author Cajas Ordonez; study itself not read.
